rail_guard.text: Lancaster Station. Trains for every station you have visited in England, Wales and Scotland. Mind the gap, the step, and the lad with the clipboard.

lan_student.text: Lancaster University is a campus on a hill outside town, and the buses are the only thing that hold it together. It opened in 1964 and the campus is a bit concrete, but the people are lovely.
The city has a legend: the Pendle witches were held in the castle. I hear a lot of people, in the town, pretending not to be descended from them.

lan_boater.text: Our boat's called Wet Weekend. I've had it eleven years, and it hasn't been dry for any of them.
The canal runs fifty-seven miles with no locks, which means you sit on the back all day and watch the cows. The cows watch back.

lan_guide.text: Welcome to the castle! The oldest bit is the Norman keep. The newest bit is the gift shop. Mind the steps, they're original.
The Pendle witches of 1612 were held here before their trial. The history is sad, and so is the weather. But the tour is warm, and the tea is hot.

lan_baker.text: Lancashire hotpot: lamb, onions, sliced potato on top, and a long, slow bake. It's the Sunday dinner of the north. I've been told I make it too well, which has never once been a complaint.
We sell Eccles cakes, too, though they're from down the road. Don't tell the Eccles people.

lan_walker.text: Lancaster's the gateway north. Fell country is that way, with the Lakes at the end of it. Wear boots. The Lakes have opinions about trainers.
From Lancaster you can see the hills across Morecambe Bay. On a clear day. Today is... a day.
